# Handle-scoped sorts still claim body gestures

## Context

While validating the operator's header-only Accounts request in neomjs/neo-agent-institution#601, a real-browser control pair showed that a narrower `dragHandleSelector` stops App-worker sorting but still suppresses ordinary body selection.

On Engine `ba0341809a680986cd65087aebd8100428e9f334` (the relevant marker/sensor sources are unchanged from `6e19f603`):

| Configuration | Native drag guard on body press | Selected body text | App sort state |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Distinct header selector, automatic outer marker retained | true | empty | index -1, no window drag |
| Same selector/header, only automatic outer marker removed | false | `Select these ordinary ` | index -1, no window drag |

The same widget's marked header still tears out in the control. Removing the outer marker once is a diagnostic, not a durable fix: construction, items-created and insertion restore it.

## The Problem

The browser claims the whole pane before the App worker rejects the gesture. A consumer-only selector change therefore fails the body-interaction requirement even when it prevents an accidental popup.

Design authority: `src/draggable/container/SortZone.mjs` documents that when a handle is specified, “the drag is initiated on this element, but the owning component is dragged.” The operator also explicitly requires body interactions to remain normal. The selection guard introduced for legitimate drags in `#16362` must remain effective.

## The Architectural Reality

- `container/DragZone.adjustItemCls` and `onItemInsert` project `neo-draggable` onto every admitted item's wrapper.
- `container/SortZone.isDraggableItem` tests handle membership; `onDragStart` checks the event path later.
- `main/draggable/sensor/Mouse.onMouseDown` finds a marked ancestor and immediately adds `neo-drag-active`. Touch uses the same marker boundary.
- The construction-time zone registry cannot alone gate the first press: container zones can have no `dragElement` until App-side drag start.

## The Fix

Separate sortable membership from automatic outer-marker eligibility at the existing container drag-zone projection boundary. For a distinct descendant handle, preserve the authored native handle marker without making the whole item a native drag target. Use the same decision for initial marking and inserted items. Preserve whole-item operation and root-handle selectors; do not remove the selection guard or introduce a Mouse-only workaround.

| Target surface | Source of authority | Proposed behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Existing `dragHandleSelector` | SortZone config JSDoc | A distinct descendant handle does not make its body a native drag target | Existing null/default whole-item and root-handle modes stay compatible | Owning marker/selector JSDoc | Native body-selection negative and header positive controls |
| Protected `isItemRootDragTarget(item)` / automatic `neo-draggable` projection | Existing DragZone construction/insertion ownership | One root-marker decision, independent of `isDraggableItem` membership; overridden by SortZone for distinct handles | Null, legacy marker and root-handle modes remain compatible; authored descendant markers remain consumer-owned | Both protected methods' JSDoc | Initial, insertion, mode-change and root-handle unit controls |

Decision Record impact: none; restores the existing handle boundary, with no new service or wire contract. Existing Body class ownership; no new production module or directory.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] With a distinct descendant handle, pressing/dragging ordinary body text does not enter the native drag guard; selection and controls remain usable and no pane drag starts.
- [ ] The same item's marked header still admits a real drag, with normal guard cleanup on release.
- [ ] Initial/items-created and inserted items follow the same marker rule. Generic whole-item dragging, the legacy default marker, root tab-header handles, resize/native-drag ownership and Touch's marker boundary remain intact.
- [ ] A browser regression fails on the original automatic outer marker and passes on the repair; focused marker units and relevant drag regressions pass.

## Out of Scope

Accounts' consumer selector change and installed FM acceptance (Institution `#601`), popup-close restoration (`#19462`), new synchronous sensor metadata, CSS selection overrides, and unrelated drag refactors.

Validation receipt: the permanent `HeaderHandleAdmissionNL.spec.mjs` passes for both initially configured and dynamically inserted panes. Body text selection, clicking/typing in an input, and scrolling remain native; the marked header still starts sorting and its selection guard releases normally.

Mutation control: restoring the two original outer-marker decisions makes the same browser spec fail because the initial pane's body press is claimed (`true` instead of `false`). The fix was restored byte-for-byte afterward. The earlier diagnostic also proved that removing only the outer marker restores selection while header tear-out remains operable.

Compatibility browser bundle: **10/10** across the new interaction witness, tab-header actions, grid header resize and cross-region column drag. Focused unit bundle: **99/99** across marker membership, tab sort, grid sort, Mouse/Touch and native HTML drag-source controls. Full unit suite: **4,844 passed, 2 skipped**.

The repair introduces `isItemRootDragTarget()` as the protected marker-projection decision; sortable membership remains `isDraggableItem()`. Initial marking and insertion call the same predicate. A distinct descendant handle does not mark the body; null, legacy `.neo-draggable`, and actual root-handle selectors retain their behavior. No sensor filter, CSS workaround or consumer helper is added. neomjs/neo-agent-institution#601 remains the consumer/installed acceptance leaf.
